extracted.intended_audience: petitioners and counsel filing post-grant review (PTAB) petitions before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and content standards for petitions seeking post-grant review of a patent under 37 CFR § 42.204, including standing, identification of challenged claims, statutory grounds, claim construction, evidentiary support, and permitted clerical corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with other procedural sections (§§ 42.6, 42.8, 42.22, 42.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the requirements of §§ 42.6, 42.8, 42.22, and 42.24, the petition must set forth the specified content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must ensure the petition also satisfies the procedural and content requirements set forth in those referenced sections (e.g., service, page limits, fee/payment, required forms or declarations) in addition to the specific content listed in § 42.204.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for standing (certification of availability and non-bar/estoppel)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must certify that the patent for which review is sought is available for post-grant review and that the petitioner is not barred or estopped from requesting a post-grant review challenging the patent claims on the grounds identified in the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an explicit certification regarding availability of post-grant review and affirmatively state that no statutory or equitable bar/estoppel prevents the petition; failure to certify standing may result in dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of precise relief requested for each claim challenged
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a statement of the precise relief requested for each claim challenged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each claim you challenge, state exactly what relief you seek (e.g., cancellation of the claim, amendment, specific claim constructions leading to unpatentability). This statement frames the requested outcome for each challenged claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the specific claim(s) challenged
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement must identify the following: (1) The claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly identify claim numbers (or language) being challenged so the Board and patent owner can unambiguously know which claims are at issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of specific statutory grounds (35 U.S.C. 282(b)(2) or (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement must identify the specific statutory grounds permitted under 35 U.S.C. 282(b)(2) or (3) on which the challenge to the claim is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the exact statutory basis for each challenged claim (e.g., anticipation, obviousness, written description, enablement, indefiniteness) as permitted by the cited provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction and corresponding specification disclosure (including 35 U.S.C. 112(f) means/step-plus-function)
rubrics_metrics.description: How the challenged claim is to be construed. Where the claim to be construed contains a means-plus-function or step-plus-function limitation as permitted under 35 U.S.C. 112(f), the construction of the claim must identify the specific portions of the specification that describe the structure, material, or acts corresponding to each claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide your proposed constructions for the claim elements. For 112(f) limitations, identify the particular specification passages that disclose the structure/material/acts that correspond to each claimed function; failure to identify supporting specification text may undermine the construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation why the construed claim is unpatentable under identified grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: How the construed claim is unpatentable under the statutory grounds identified in paragraph (b)(2) of this section. Where the grounds for unpatentability are based on prior art, the petition must specify where each element of the claim is found in the prior art. For all other grounds of unpatentability, the petition must identify the specific part of the claim that fails to comply with the statutory grounds raised and state how the identified subject matter fails to comply with the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When alleging unpatentability: (a) if based on prior art, map each claim element to specific portions of the prior art references (with citations); (b) for other statutory grounds (e.g., enablement, written description, indefiniteness), identify the exact claim text and explain how it fails to meet the statutory requirement. General or conclusory assertions without element-by-element mapping or specific identification are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibits: identification of exhibit numbers and statement of relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: The exhibit number of the supporting evidence relied upon to support the challenge and the relevance of the evidence to the challenge raised, including identifying specific portions of the evidence that support the challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List exhibit numbers for each piece of supporting evidence and explain how each exhibit supports particular claim elements or arguments, pointing to specific pages/lines/figures. Note: the Board may exclude or give no weight to evidence where a party has failed to state its relevance or to identify specific portions of the evidence that support the challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to correct clerical or typographical mistakes in the petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion may be filed that seeks to correct a clerical or typographical mistake in the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you discover clerical/typographical mistakes after filing, you may file a motion to correct them; however, grant of such a motion does not change the petition's filing date, so do not rely on correction to alter timeliness or priority.
